{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2020}}
The '''Professorship of Mathematical Statistics''' at the [[University of Cambridge]] was established in 1961<ref>{{Citation |  title=Statutes and Ordinances of University of Cambridge | url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/so/pdfs }}</ref> with the support of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] and the aid of donations from various companies and banks.<ref>{{cite journal | year = 1962 | title = Annual Report of the Council | journal = [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series A (General)]] | volume = 125 | issue = 4 | pages = 605–625 | publisher = Wiley for the Royal Statistical Society | jstor = 2982621}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | first1=P. | last1=Whittle | authorlink=Peter Whittle (mathematician) | title=The Cambridge Statistical Laboratory up to 1993 (revised 2002) | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html | access-date=28 April 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219080017/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html | archive-date=19 December 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref> It was the first professorship in the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge|Statistical Laboratory]], and the first in [[Cambridge University]] explicitly intended for the study of statistics. Until 1973 the professor was ''[[ex officio]]'' Director of the Statistical Laboratory.

==List of professors of mathematical statistics==
* 1962&ndash;1985 [[David George Kendall|David Kendall]]
* 1985&ndash;1992 [[David Williams (mathematician)|David Williams]]
* 1992&ndash; [[Geoffrey Grimmett]]
